title: Sugar transport in ripening fruit
summary: A nodulin MtN21/EamA-like transporter expressed specifically in late-fruit vascular bundles. DOF5.1 (highly expressed, 353 TPM) actively regulates this gene. Silencing via H3K4me1 removal would reduce sugar loading into ripening fruit — a direct lever for controlling sweetness and Brix content.

title: Flavonoid biosynthesis in carpels
summary: An aromatic compound catabolic enzyme in the flavonoid pathway. RVE4 shows near-perfect co-expression (ρ=0.93). Activating this gene in carpels would boost anthocyanin pigmentation — directly relevant to fruit color, consumer appeal, and antioxidant content.

title: Seed nutrient storage (acetoacetyl-CoA reductase)
summary: An acetoacetyl-CoA reductase controlling lipid biosynthesis in seeds. Highly cell-type-specific (tau=0.88, epidermis). Activating via H3K36me3 would enhance seed oil content and nutritional value — relevant for strawberry breeding programs focused on achene quality.

title: DREB2F stress-responsive target in late fruit
summary: Regulated by the drought-responsive DREB2F transcription factor. Cell-type-specific in late fruit (tau=0.52). Activating would enhance stress tolerance during the critical fruit maturation phase — protecting yield under heat/drought conditions.

title: Developmental signaling in fruit ripening
summary: An ATP-binding signaling kinase controlling anatomical development. Silencing in late fruit via H3K36me3 would modulate ripening timing — enabling delayed harvest for better shelf life or synchronized ripening for mechanical harvesting.

title: Methyltransferase for pollen fertility
summary: A methyltransferase specifically expressed in anthers, controlling pollen development. Activating would enhance male fertility — critical for F1 hybrid seed production in commercial strawberry breeding.
